front.title: A Backpressure Algorithm for Sender-Side Track Switching in MOQ Transport

abstract.t: Sender-Side Track Switching (SSTS) lets a publisher forward one track at a time out of a switching set, and leaves the choice of which track to a pluggable algorithm. The default algorithm divides a bandwidth estimate between switching sets. This document defines an alternative algorithm that uses no bandwidth estimate at all. It monitors the number of open forwarding streams carrying the currently active tier, steps rapidly through the switching set's ladder during fast start, regulates steady-state upshifts dynamically according to relative bitrate jumps and the subscriber's probing risk tolerance, and reacts to mid-group congestion using intra-group monitoring and retroactive stream supersede. The signal is directly observable at the publisher, requires no cooperation from the congestion controller, and degrades toward the lowest quality under load rather than toward none.
